comments.body: Implemented in decb92b (native_frontmatter: <target> on a source; fits decision 14 since fields reach only the named target).
comments.author: Alexander Terp

creator: Alexander Terp
description:
Installing a third-party skill pack (13 skills written for Claude Code, staged into a local source by the pack's own installer) prints one warning per skill:

```
skill "<name>": frontmatter field "allowed-tools" is not a tai field and was not installed - claude will not see it. Move it under 'native.claude' to pass it through in claude's own format.
```

and the skills install without their tool restriction. "Move it under native.claude" is not available for files tai doesn't own: honoring it means 13 patch files, each re-blessed on every upstream release, to restore a field Claude reads natively anyway. I accepted the loss, so every install now prints 13 warnings.

Suggested, either:

- Let a source (or a bundle entry) declare that its assets' unknown frontmatter is a given target's own, e.g. `native_frontmatter: claude` on the source in tai.yaml, and pass those fields through verbatim.
- Or map the fields tai already knows a target reads (the tai skill lists Claude's: `disable-model-invocation`, `user-invocable`, `allowed-tools`, `effort`, `argument-hint`, `paths`, `hooks`) into `native.<target>` instead of dropping them. Dropping loses information tai could have forwarded.

(Moved from GitHub issue #9.)
title: Pass target-native frontmatter through for skills from a source you don't own
